items.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence: Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found and exploited a MONAI Label zero-day
items.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses with moderate confidence that a Chinese-nexus actor gave autonomous agents built on the open-source Cairn framework the goal of obtaining shell access against East Asian university IPs over about 48 hours from 8 Sept 2026. AWS found the actor's unauthenticated Cairn instance exposing prompts and outputs; the agents independently found a path traversal arbitrary-file-write flaw in MONAI Label, assessed with high confidence as a zero-day, and used it to obtain a root reverse shell. Other agent operations against Redis and a GPU server failed.

items.title: MONAI Label GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94: path traversal in datastore upload endpoints allows arbitrary file write (<= 0.8.5)
items.summary: Critical advisory for the monailabel pip package, versions <= 0.8.5, with no CVE assigned: path traversal in datastore upload endpoints allows arbitrary file write. The fix is in PR #1915 and is slated for the next release; workarounds are enabling authentication, restricting network exposure and running as an unprivileged user. Reported via the AWS security VDP.

items.title: GAO-27-108458: AI and Cybersecurity - technologies can magnify cyberattacks and enhance cyber defense
items.summary: US GAO technology assessment finding that AI magnifies traditional attacks such as phishing, deepfakes and agentic AI executing multiple attack stages with minimal human input, while defenders face missing evaluation criteria, new attack surface, fragmented regulation and poor data sharing. It sets out 16 policy options under four goals: guidance and practices, research gaps, lifecycle governance of AI tools, and workforce.

items.title: Cursor incident: stolen Fireworks AI key and coding-agent traces led to trojanized Claude Code extension copies in Cursor's marketplace cache
items.summary: Cursor says an attacker used an access key issued to Fireworks to copy a read-only bucket of mostly 2025 non-Privacy-Mode coding-agent traces, then pivoted via credentials to SaaS tools and on 29 Oct 2026 placed malicious copies of the Anthropic.claude-code extension (2.1.312/2.1.313) in the cache serving its VS Code marketplace. At most 5,000 users may have received the build, live about 11 hours; secondary reporting says it attempted to install a persistent SSH backdoor. Cursor rotated credentials, rebuilt the marketplace and says uninstalling alone may not be enough.

items.title: Brazil: AI-generated fake stores and fake Pix payments flagged as Black Friday fraud vectors
items.summary: Brazilian regional outlet Correio warns of AI-made fake stores, cloned sites and fake Pix payments ahead of Black Friday, citing a Reclame AQUI survey and the 20th Anuario Brasileiro de Seguranca Publica on fear of fraud. Consumer advice only; no specific incident data or primary threat-intelligence source.

items.title: Langflow 1.0.0-1.12.8: unauthenticated auth bypass and code execution (CVE-2026-93680, CVE-2026-110186) plus two authenticated flaws; fixed in 1.13.0
items.summary: Per The Hacker News, citing an IBM security bulletin of 28 Oct 2026, Langflow 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 is affected by CVE-2026-93680 (CVSS 9.8 auth bypass) and CVE-2026-110186 (CVSS 9.8 code execution) without an account, plus CVE-2026-110193 (8.8, OS commands via the Agentic Assistant) and CVE-2026-110192 (6.5). The only fix is 1.13.0, which also disables default auto-login; a public Metasploit auxiliary module references CVE-2026-93680, and no in-the-wild exploitation or KEV listing is reported. Primary IBM bulletin not read in this run.

items.title: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms (arXiv 2611.11861)
items.summary: Kurakin et al. argue prompt injection remains feasible even as human red teaming saturates; a synthetic dataset uses benign random actions as attacker goals to measure instruction-hierarchy adherence. A more capable agentic attacker reliably makes models follow instructions in tool output, including models considered robust on public benchmarks such as GraySwan Arena. The abstract gives no numeric results.

items.title: SearchInject: retrieval exposure control for indirect prompt injection in LLM search (arXiv 2611.02643)
items.summary: Defense that scores candidate pages for relevance, search-abuse cues and instruction likelihood and quarantines them before they reach a search-augmented LLM. On 300 SciFact queries it cuts top-10 exposure of injected pages by about 83% across BM25, hybrid and LSA retrievers with negligible nDCG change, but clean false-quarantine (0.59-0.65%) exceeded the 0.5% target and no attack-success reduction was estimated.

items.title: INFUSE: unified surface benchmark for indirect prompt injection in agentic systems (arXiv 2610.20776)
items.summary: Benchmark of 40 long-horizon tasks and 56 attack scenarios injected through interaction surfaces, evaluated on 19 LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Gemma, Qwen) over 41,824 adversarial trajectories. Mean attack success is 15.4-19.6% depending on the judge, ranging 3.2-41.9% per model; guard models helped little, while prompt-level instructional hardening cut mean success from 58.2% to 14.3%.

items.title: Zenity Labs AgentCorruption: single prompt to an exposed AWS Bedrock AgentCore agent pulled metadata-service credentials
items.summary: Per the Adversa AI November 2026 roundup, Zenity Labs showed that one prompt to an exposed Bedrock AgentCore agent could retrieve cloud metadata-service credentials, and AWS has patched it. The Zenity original was not read in this run; date is the roundup's.

items.title: EMBRACE: embedded browsers in AI coding assistants break core browser isolation (Cursor, Copilot, Codex, VS Code, Claude Desktop)
items.summary: Per the Adversa AI November 2026 roundup, forever.security found embedded browsers in five AI assistants that violate a core browser security rule, exposing a path to developer secrets; Cursor and Copilot are reported fixed, Codex and VS Code unpatched, and no fix stated for Claude Desktop. Original not read in this run.

items.title: Datadog Security Labs: counterfeit policy steers an LLM-as-judge prompt-injection classifier (recall 83% to under 4%)
items.summary: Per the Adversa AI November 2026 roundup, Datadog showed that injecting a counterfeit policy reduced the Jev classifier's prompt-injection recall from 83% to under 4%. Original not read in this run.

items.title: Visual Studio Copilot and SSMS remote code execution via trailing-dot .mcp.json filename check bypass (CVE-2026-103572)
items.summary: Per the Adversa AI coding-agent roundup of 2 Nov 2026, Johann Rehberger found that a trailing dot in a filename bypassed a protection check on MCP configuration in a shared Copilot DLL, enabling command execution in Visual Studio (including 2022) and SQL Server Management Studio; Microsoft rated it Important and patched it. Original not read in this run.
